name: Human review queue
problem: Every automation worth deploying has a residue — the cases only a person can judge. Untended, the residue accumulates into the backlog that discredits the whole system: 'the automation doesn't work, Marcus still does it all by hand.' The queue is where deployments actually die, and they die of staffing, not code.
signals: An automation exists or is planned, and someone says 'and the weird ones go to...' without finishing the sentence.
Exception handling is described as a person's name rather than a process.
Escalations arrive by someone walking over to a desk.
not_for: The 'residue' is most of the volume. Then the automation's core is not working, and a queue just relabels the old manual process with extra steps.
Judgments that must happen in seconds. That is staffing for real-time operations, not a queue — a queue's unit of time is the working session.

steps: An item enters carrying full machine context: why it fell out, the machine's best guess with its confidence, and links to the source record and document.
It lands in one queue, with entry time and age visible — parallel side-channels are how items get lost.
The operator resolves it with a structured outcome — match-to-X, reject-junk, escalate, new-case-type — never free text alone.
The outcome writes back to the parent flow as both the resolution and a labeled training example.
Depth and age alarms fire from the flow itself when the queue stops being worked.
base_shape.state: The queue itself, per-item machine context, and the outcome history. The outcome history is the most valuable dataset the deployment produces — it is the ground truth for every threshold in the parent flow.
commitments: One queue. The moment exceptions also flow through DMs and hallway asks, the queue is fiction and its metrics are lies.
Machine context travels with the item. An operator who must re-derive what the machine knew is doing the work twice.
The queue is a staffed role with a named backup. This pattern treats bus-factor-one as a defect, not a fact of life.
Alarms belong to the flow, not to the operator's diligence. The queue must be able to complain about being ignored.

variation_points.question: Where does the queue physically live?

options.when: One operator, and the intake channel already marks state — unread mail, an unmoved file.
options.consequence: The smallest possible build: zero UI, the channel is the queue. Age and depth must still be measured from outside.

options.when: Multiple operators, no build budget — a sheet or board the team already uses.
options.consequence: Cheap coordination; state drifts from reality unless the flow writes to it, not just people.

options.when: SLA reporting, multiple operators, or outcome capture justify a built surface.
options.consequence: Best data and habits; a real build with real maintenance, so make it earn its keep first.

variation_points.default_because: Start with zero UI — the reference deployment runs its queue as unread mail. The queue's own data tells you when it has outgrown the channel; building the view first is guessing.

variation_points.question: How is the set of structured outcomes chosen?

options.when: Nearly always — you do not yet know the case taxonomy.
options.consequence: Start with three or four outcomes plus 'other'; when 'other' exceeds roughly 15%, the vocabulary is missing a word and the queue data names it.

options.when: The case types are genuinely known — a regulated process with enumerated exception codes.
options.consequence: Clean data from day one; wrong categories from day one if the enumeration was aspirational.

variation_points.default_because: Taxonomies designed before contact with real cases classify imagined cases. Let 'other' accumulate, then read it — it is the cheapest user research the deployment will ever get.

variation_points.question: Where does the queue's SLA come from?

options.when: Always, when a real downstream tolerance exists.
options.consequence: The SLA inherits from the manifest's tolerable_downtime — the queue may back up exactly as long as the business genuinely does not feel it.

options.when: No measurable downstream tolerance exists yet.
options.consequence: Pick a number and mark it provisional; an ambitious SLA nobody resources becomes a dashboard everyone learns to ignore.

variation_points.default_because: SLAs derived from what the business can actually absorb get staffed; SLAs derived from ambition get ignored, and an ignored SLA teaches people to ignore the queue.

glue_checklist.question: Who operates the queue, when are they away, and does the cover person know they are the cover?
glue_checklist.why_it_matters: The reference deployment's queue reverted cold to a supervisor when its operator left the company — a two-week backlog, and the origin of this pattern's named-backup requirement. An uninformed backup is a name on a page.
glue_checklist.recorded_in: flows[].lineage (operator and backup-operator tenures) and walkthroughs

glue_checklist.question: How long can the queue back up before the business feels it?
glue_checklist.why_it_matters: This number is the SLA's parent and the alarm threshold's parent. Without it, both are decoration.

glue_checklist.question: Are resolutions being captured anywhere today, in any form?
glue_checklist.why_it_matters: If outcomes go nowhere, the queue never shrinks — the parent flow cannot learn from judgments it never sees. Capture from day one, even unmined.
glue_checklist.recorded_in: flows[].steps (the outcome write-back) and handoff.recommended_next if deferred

glue_checklist.question: Who has the authority to say the queue is overloaded, and what happens when they do?
glue_checklist.why_it_matters: Queue overload is a staffing decision, not an engineering one. The escalation path must reach someone who can assign people — the space's decision maker, not the steward.

human_roles.does: Works the queue on its cadence; resolves items with structured outcomes; flags shifts in what the queue contains.
human_roles.cadence: Daily, a bounded session — if the queue does not fit in the session, that is an alarm, not overtime.
transition_walkthrough_must_cover: A paired live session on real items — shadow one session, run the next reversed.
The outcome vocabulary and the judgment line between each pair of outcomes.
What the machine context means, and which parts of it to distrust.
The escalation path, and the fact that escalating is always a safe move.

human_roles.does: Covers planned and unplanned absence. Required by the pattern — an unfilled backup role is a recorded risk, not an acceptable configuration.
human_roles.cadence: At least one real session per quarter, so the coverage is exercised rather than theoretical.
transition_walkthrough_must_cover: The same walkthrough as the operator — no abbreviated version.
How to tell the primary operator what happened during coverage, so context does not fork.

human_roles.does: Mines the outcome history: tunes parent-flow thresholds, extends the vocabulary when 'other' grows, and proposes automation for case types that have become routine.
human_roles.cadence: Monthly review of outcome distribution; ad hoc when the operator flags a shift.
transition_walkthrough_must_cover: How outcome data feeds each threshold in the parent flow.
The history of vocabulary changes and why each word was added.
Which case types are trending toward automatable, and what evidence would justify it.

failure_design.failure: The queue quietly stops being worked — absence, reassignment, or simple drift.
failure_design.response: Depth and age alarms routed to a channel the space's decision maker sees. Staffing failures escalate to the person who can assign staff, because the steward cannot fix this with code.

failure_design.failure: A poison item re-enters the queue on every replay or restart.
failure_design.response: Resolutions are sticky: an item resolved 'reject' must stay resolved across replays, keyed by the same identity the dedup uses.

failure_design.failure: Outcome data is captured as free text and becomes unminable.
failure_design.response: Structured outcomes from day one, with free text as an optional annotation. The structure is what makes the queue a dataset instead of a diary.

manifest_bindings.systems: Wherever the queue lives — the channel, tracker, or built view — with access and the gotchas of using it as a queue.
manifest_bindings.entities: Inherited from the parent flow; the queue adds no entities, only judgments about existing ones.

decisions_expected.tension: Zero-build channel reuse versus data quality and multi-operator coordination.

decisions_expected.topic: The SLA and its alarm thresholds
decisions_expected.tension: Downstream tolerance versus ambition — and who is on the hook when the alarm fires.

constraints_expected: Any sensitivity constraint on queue contents — review queues concentrate exactly the documents that are confidential.

metrics.note: Measured against the SLA, which is derived from downstream tolerance, not ambition.

metrics.metric: Queue entries as percent of parent-flow volume
metrics.note: The queue shrinking is the automation improving. This is the single best number for the health of the whole deployment.
Above roughly 15%, the outcome vocabulary is missing a word — read the 'other' annotations and add it.

deviations: Lives directly in the mailbox as unread mail — the leave-in-channel option at its most minimal.
Outcome capture is partial: resolutions happen but are not yet structured, recorded upstream as a recommended next step.
The backup-operator role went unfilled, and the resulting two-week backlog is why this pattern now requires it.

maturity.evidence: Extracted from one deployment where it ran as a sub-component of document intake, plus one painful staffing transition that shaped the backup-operator requirement. The alarm thresholds and the 15% 'other' heuristic are placeholders until more instantiations exist.
